Its former rank under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=Modern shrine ranking system}} was prefectural shrine. {{nihongo|'''Noki Shrine'''|能義神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumo Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
Current deities are as follows.
*{{ill|Ame no Hohi|bg|Аме Но Хохи|fa|آمه-نو-هوهی|fr|Ame no Hohi|it|Ame no Hohi|ja|アメノホヒ|pl|Niebiański Duch Przewodni|ru|Амэ но Хохи|simple|Ame no Hohi|zh|天菩比神|qid=Q10940685|lt=Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto}}
*{{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto}}
*{{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto}}
In the entry for Noki station in Ou District of the ''{{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|de|Izumo Fudoki|ja|出雲国風土記|simple|Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki|zh|出雲國風土記|qid=Q11395858}}'', Noki Ōkami appears. The original deity is considered to have been this Noki Ōkami, and there is a theory that Noki Ōkami and Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto are the same deity<ref name="bunken2">''Gods of Japan (7)'', p.40.</ref>.

== History ==
It is identified with “Noki-sha,” a Shrine Bureau shrine in the Ou District section of ''Izumo-no-Kuni Fudoki,'' and with “Noki Shrine” in Ou District, Izumo Province, in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}''; but there is also a theory identifying it with “Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto Shrine” in Nogi District in the same text. Between this shrine and Kunitsu Daimyōjin in Kisa village (now {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shibusa Shrine}}), there were disputes over candidate status twice: in the {{ill|Shōtoku (era)|Q1193848|qid=Q1193848|lt=Shōtoku}} era and early {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}<ref>''Gods of Japan (7)'', p.42.</ref>.

According to ''{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}'', the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} granted to Nogi deity was Junior Fifth Upper in {{ill|Dizzy (series)|be_x_old|Dizzy|cs|Dizzy|es|Dizzy|fr|Dizzy (série de jeux vidéo)|it|Dizzy (serie)|pl|Dizzy (seria)|ro|Dizzy (serie de jocuri)|ru|Dizzy (серия игр)|sk|Dizzy|qid=Q23899}} ({{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635}} 9) and Senior Fifth Lower in {{ill|Tworki, Siedlce County|ce|Творки (Седлецкан повет)|fr|Tworki (Siedlce)|pl|Tworki (powiat siedlecki)|szl|Tworki (śedlecki krys)|tt|Творки (Седлецкий повяты)|uk|Творкі (Седлецький повіт)|zh_min_nan|Tworki (Siedlce Kūn)|qid=Q23903}} (Jōgan 13). However, it is unclear whether these were granted to Noki Shrine or to Ame-no-Hohi-no-Mikoto Shrine<ref name="bunken2" />.

When shrine buildings were lost in a fire in {{ill|1611|Q6768|qid=Q6768}} ({{ill|Keichō|ca|Keichō|es|Keichō|fa|کیچو (دوره)|fr|Ère Keichō|id|Keichō|it|Keichō|ja|慶長|ko|게이초|ru|Кэйтё|simple|Keichō|sr|Кеичо|sv|Keichō|th|เคโช|tr|Keichō|uk|Кейтьо|zh|慶長|qid=Q1328185}} 16), old records were also lost. In early modern times it was revered as the sōsha of Nogi District. It was ranked gōsha in {{ill|Meiji – year 4|Q11512280|qid=Q11512280}}, then promoted to prefectural shrine in Meiji 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}).

== Ancient historic sites ==
In the precinct is the Noki Shrine site, considered to be dwelling remains from the {{ill|Yayoi period|Q207858|qid=Q207858}} to {{ill|Kofun period|Q459939|qid=Q459939}}. Nearby are several {{ill|Round Kofun|ja|円墳|simple|Round Kofun|zh|圓墳|qid=Q11394747}}, including Noki Shrine Okuin Kofun.
